summary: ts-node crashes on TypeScript 7 because the compiler API is no longer exported via require('typescript').
context: The developer upgraded a project to TypeScript 7.0.2 (an ESM-only release) but left ts-node in the scripts, which breaks because it relies on the CommonJS exports of the compiler API.
setup: mkdir -p /w && cd /w && npm init -y && npm install typescript@7.0.2 ts-node@10.9.2 && echo "const x: number = 1; console.log(x);" > index.ts
fix_command: cd /w && npm uninstall ts-node && npm install tsx@4.23.15
root_cause: TypeScript 7.0 removed the synchronous compiler API from the default CommonJS export of 'typescript' (it only exports a version string). Tools like ts-node that rely on 'require("typescript")' exposing 'ts.sys' crash with undefined property errors.
steps: Identify that ts-node is incompatible with the TypeScript 7.0 ESM-only API.
Replace ts-node with tsx, a modern esbuild-powered alternative for executing TypeScript.
Update execution scripts to use tsx instead of ts-node.
